observationsNotFindings.observation: The two turn-2 requiredRepairs proposed mutually exclusive literal strings for the same sentence: Claude 'Does not unwrite the turn-1 OBJECT.' and Codex 'Does not unwrite the turn-1 Claude OBJECT.' Line 209 takes the Codex string and appends 'or the turn-2 OBJECTs.' The second clause of the frozen Claude reLandCheck ('Does not unwrite the turn-1 OBJECT.' present) is therefore not literally met: grep -c 'turn-1 OBJECT' returns 0, grep -c 'turn-1 Claude OBJECT' returns 1.
observationsNotFindings.whyNotAFinding: Both literal repairs could not be satisfied at once; the Codex string is a strict specialisation of the Claude string (singular, plus the reviewer name that the subject's own line 76 gives). The defect named by CLAUDE-D283-T2-SF1 - a plural with no referent set - is gone; 'the turn-1 Claude OBJECT' resolves to exactly one frozen verdict (7f3b9002...). The appended 'the turn-2 OBJECTs' has an exact two-member referent set (823add97..., 12dd3ec3...) recited at lines 103-104, so it introduces no new plural defect. Same standard this reviewer applied at CLAUDE-D283-T2-O1 (turn-1 literal 'G09 occupancy v4' vs landed 'occupancy v4'). Landed; not re-landed here.
